The crash is fixed. The cause was a bug in `Text` itself, not in `inspect`, and new tests cover it.

**Cause:** `Text.__init__` (`rich/text.py:144`) removes a few control characters from the string: backspace, vertical tab, form feed and carriage return (`\r`). But it set `_length` from the original string, so the text's recorded length was longer than its actual content. Docstrings with Windows `\r\n` line endings, like some in pyparsing, hit this. `inspect` passes them through the highlighter, which builds `Text(str)`. The highlight positions are then measured against the cleaned string while `divide()` works from the wrong length, and it reads past the end of its list of lines, raising the `IndexError` in the traceback. Any `Text` built from a string containing those characters had the wrong length, so the fix applies beyond `inspect`.

**Fix:** `_length` is now computed from the cleaned string (a two-line change in `rich/text.py`).

**Tests:**
- `tests/test_text.py::test_strip_control_codes` now also checks `len(text)` after the control codes are removed.
- New `tests/test_inspect.py::test_inspect_method_with_control_codes_in_docstring` inspects a class whose method docstring contains `\r\n`, with `methods=True`.
- Both tests fail on the original code and pass with the fix. pyparsing isn't installed in the venv, so I reproduced the issue with a synthetic `\r\n` docstring rather than the original command.

**Test suite:** 17 tests fail across the whole suite, and the same 17 fail on the unmodified code. They are 3 in `test_inspect.py` and others in `test_syntax.py`. The ones I looked at come from Python 3.12 output differences, such as built-in `print`'s signature rendering differently. The fix adds no new failures.

I also added a line to the Unreleased section of `CHANGELOG.md`. I didn't put an issue number in it because I don't know the right one, so you may want to add it.

One quirk remains: a `\r\n\r\n` paragraph break isn't recognised by `_first_paragraph`, so with `help=False` a CRLF docstring shows in full instead of only its first paragraph. It no longer crashes. Fixing that would mean normalising line endings in `rich/_inspect.py`, which I left out to keep this change small.

Nothing has been committed.
